newsitem.title: USA: SBC offering notes linked to Telmex ADS.
newsitem.headline: SBC offering notes linked to Telmex ADS.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc said Thursday it plans to offer four-year notes exchangeable into American Depository Shares (ADSs) of Telfonos de Mexico SA (Telmex).
At maturity, holders of the debt exchangeable for common stock will receive Telmex ADS or, at SBC's option, cash in lieu of the ADSs.
Telmex, the Mexican telecommunications company privatized in December 1990, is partly owned by SBC. SBC's subsidiaries include Southwestern Bell.
The number of Telmex ADSs, or the equivalent amount of cash, exchangeable at maturity will be based upon the price of Telmex ADSs shortly before the notes mature.
SBC said it plans to offer up to nine million debt exchangeable for common stock (DECS) units, 10 million if the over-allotment options is exercised in full.

It added that Telmex filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission a registration statement related to the Telmex ADSs owned by SBC that may be deliverable in connection with the note offering.
SBC currently owns AA and L shares representing 9.6 percent of the total outstanding equity of Telmex.
Each ADS related in the offering is equivalent to 20 L shares of Telmex.
The offering does not affect SBC's ownership of approximately 530 million Telmex AA shares.
"This (debt) offering is a financial, not a strategic, initiative: we remain fully committed to our investment in Telmex," Donald Kiernan, SBC chief financial officer, said in a statement.

The debt exchangeable for common stock will pay quarterly interest and will mature in four years, SBC said. The offering, underwritten by Salomon Brothers Inc, is expected to raise about $350 million, it added.
